```markdown
---
name: greenhouse-alerting-scope
description: Agreed scope and urgency for the greenhouse alerting service (SMS to weekly on-call person)
metadata:
  type: project
---

Alerting service for the greenhouse. Scope was agreed on 2026-10-28, during design, before any code existed.

- Reads the readings that `ingest/` writes to `greenhouse.db`. There are 12 temperature/humidity sensors, and each one reports every minute over MQTT.
- Sends a text message to the weekly on-call person when a zone leaves its safe range.
- Repeats the alert every 15 minutes until someone acknowledges it.
- Raises an alert when a sensor is silent for 10 minutes.
- Out of scope: dashboards, history reports.

**Why:** If the heater fails on a January night, the seedlings die in about 2 hours. The alert must wake a person. A morning record is not enough.

**How to apply:** Judge design choices against the 2-hour window. Treat missed or late alerts as the main failure, not noisy ones. See [[greenhouse-safe-ranges]] once that is known.
```

Good, the scope is set. Next we need to know what "out of range" means, because every alert depends on it.

**What are the safe ranges, and are they the same for all twelve sensors?** Give me the low and high limits for temperature and for humidity. If zones differ, tell me which sensor is in which zone. A seedling bench may need different limits from a bench of mature plants.

Also tell me if you want a warning level before the critical level. For example, a warning text at 10 °C and an urgent alert at 7 °C. If not, we keep one level.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- A sensor value that sits close to a limit can cross it again and again, and each crossing raises an alert. A small dead band stops that. For example, the alert starts below 7 °C and clears only above 8 °C. I will propose one after I know your limits.
- Your 2-hour loss window sets the timing budget. The 10-minute stale check plus a 15-minute repeat leaves time for a second text before the risk grows. A warning level would add more margin.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

After the ranges, I have two more open questions. They are how someone acknowledges an alert and where the on-call rota comes from. I will ask them one at a time.
